πληγὴν, καθὰ τὸ ἱερόν φησι γράμμα, ἔδει καὶ τοὺς παῖδας διπλῶς εἶναι. Σκόπει γὰρ
ἐπὶ τῶν κτηνῶν· πρόβατα, φησὶν, ἦν αὐτῷ μύρια τε τρακισχίλια, ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀρχῇ
εἶχεν ἑπτα κισχίλια· καμήλων ἑξακισχίλια, ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀρχῇ εἶχεν τρισχίλια· ζεῦγα
βοῶν χίλια, πρῶτον γὰρ ἦσαν πεντακόσια. Τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν νομάδων ὄνων. 389
Γεννῶνται δὲ αὐτῷ, φησὶν, υἱοὶ ἑπτὰ καὶ θυγατέρες τρεῖς, ὅσοι ἦσαν καὶ πρότερον·
ἔδει δὲ τοὺς μὲν δεκατέσσαρας εἶναι, τὰς δὲ ἓξ, ἵνα εἶεν διπλοῖ τῶν ἀπολωλότων
παίδων. Λέ γομεν οὖν, ὅτι τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἀπολώλον ται, καὶ τὰ κτήνη· οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ καὶ
αἱ θυγα τέρες τεθνήκασιν, οὐκ ἀπώλοντο. Ἔδωκεν οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς καὶ ἕτερα
τοσοῦτα τέκνα, ὥστε ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει διπλᾶ ἔχειν αὐτὰ, ὥστε καὶ πατέρα διπλασίων
παίδων αὐτὸν πεποίηκεν ὁ Θεὸς, ὧν ἦν πρότερον πατήρ. Εἰ δὲ ἡ ψυχὴ ἐσβέννυτο
μετὰ θάνατον, καὶ τὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως οὐκ ἦν ἀληθῶς, ἔδει υἱοὺς δοθῆναι
δεκατέσσαρας καὶ θυγατέρας ἕξ. ∆ιὸ ἱερῶς ἡ γραφὴ τετήρηκε περὶ τοῦ ὅτι ἔλαβεν
υἱοὺς ζʹ· εἰ δὲ ἐγεγόνεισαν αὐτῷ δέκα τέσσαρες υἱοὶ καὶ θυγατέρες ἓξ, σω ζομένου
τοῦ περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως λόγου, οὐκ εἰσὶν αὐτῷ διπλᾶ δεδομένα τὰ τέκνα, ἀλλὰ
τριπλᾶ, ἢ ἦσαν δὲ πρῶτον. ι ʹ. Ἔζησε δὲ Ἰὼβ μετὰ τὴν πληγὴν ἔτη ἑκατὸν
ἑβδομήκοντα, τὰ δὲ πάντα ἔτη ἔζησεν διακόσια τεσσαράκοντα. Πῶς νοεῖται ὁ Ἰὼβ
ζήσας μετὰ τὴν πλη γὴν, ἔτη ροʹ, τῶν πάντων ὄντων τῆς ζωῆς αὐτοῦ ἐτῶν σμηʹ;
Φαμὲν τοίνυν λεπτολο γοῦντες, ὅτι πάντα τὰ ἀγαθὰ διπλᾶ ἀπο λαβὼν, ἐὰν καὶ τὰ
τῆς προτέρας εὐημερίας ἔτη διπλᾶ ἀπείληπται, οὕτως ἀριθμῆσαι προ σήκει. Ἔζησεν
ἐν τῇ προτέρᾳ εὐθηνίᾳ ἔτη οζʹ, καὶ ἀφ' οὗ τὴν πληγὴν ἐδέξατο, ἔμεινεν ἐν τῇ
κακοπαθείᾳ ἔτη ιδʹ. Οὕτως νοητέον τὸ μετὰ τὴν πληγὴν, οὐκ ἀφ' οὗ ἡ πληγὴ
ἐπαύσατο, ἀλλ' ἀφ' οὗ ἤρξατο· μετὰ δὲ τὰ τέσσαρα καὶ δέκα ἔτη, χρόνον τῆς νόσου,
pass_a_gloss: … blow (stroke), as the holy writing says, the children also should have been doubly. For consider in the case of the beasts: sheep, he says, there were to him ten thousand four thousand, for in the beginning he had seven thousand; of camels six thousand, for in the beginning he had three thousand; yoke of oxen a thousand, for first there were five hundred. The same also in the case of the pasturing asses. And there are born to him, he says, seven sons and three daughters, as many as were also before; but it was needed that the [sons] be fourteen, and the [daughters] six, so that they might be double of the lost children. We say then that the sheep have been lost (destroyed), and the beasts; but the sons and the daughters have died, they were not lost. God therefore gave him also as many other children, so that in the resurrection he has them double, so that God has made him also father of double the children of whom he was formerly father. But if the soul were quenched after death, and the matters of the resurrection were not truly, it was needed that fourteen sons be given and six daughters. Therefore holily the Scripture has guarded concerning [the fact] that he received 7 sons; but if there had been born to him fourteen sons and six daughters, the word about the resurrection being kept safe, the children are not given double to him, but triple, than they were at first. Label: verse 16 (printed 'ι ʹ', stigma lost). And Job lived after the stroke a hundred and seventy years, and all the years he lived two hundred forty. How is Job understood having lived after the stroke 170 years, all the years of his life being 248? We say therefore, speaking with subtlety, that having received back all the goods double, if also the years of the earlier prosperity he has received back double, so it is fitting to count. He lived in the former plenty 77 years, and from when he received the stroke, he remained in the hard suffering 14 years. So must be understood the 'after the stroke', not from when the stroke ceased, but from when it began; and after the four and ten years, the time of the disease, …
pass_b_english: … stroke, as the sacred writing says, then his children too ought to have been doubled. Look at the livestock: he had, it says, fourteen thousand sheep, for at the beginning he had seven thousand (Job 1:3); six thousand camels, for at the beginning he had three thousand; a thousand yoke of oxen, for at first there were five hundred. The same holds for the grazing asses. Yet seven sons and three daughters, it says, are born to him, as many as there were before (Job 1:2). But there ought to have been fourteen sons and six daughters, so that they would be double the children he lost. We say, then, that the sheep and the livestock were lost, but the sons and the daughters died; they were not lost. So God gave him as many children again, so that in the resurrection he would have them double; and so God has made him the father of twice as many children as he was father of before. But if the soul were extinguished after death, and the resurrection were not real, he would have had to be given fourteen sons and six daughters. That is why Scripture has reverently kept to the statement that he received seven sons. For if fourteen sons and six daughters had been born to him, with the teaching on the resurrection still standing, the children given to him would not be double but triple what they were at first.

“And Job lived after the stroke a hundred and seventy years, and all the years he lived were two hundred and forty” (Job 42:16). How is Job understood to have lived a hundred and seventy years after the stroke, when the whole of his life came to two hundred and forty-eight years? We say, then, reckoning closely, that since he received all his goods back double, if he also received back double the years of his former prosperity, this is how the count should be made. He lived seventy-seven years in his former plenty, and from the time he received the stroke he remained in suffering fourteen years. So “after the stroke” must be understood to mean not from when the stroke ceased but from when it began. And after the fourteen years, the time of his disease, …

choices.issue: Old English misread numbers and invented claims
choices.choice: 'thirty thousand' sheep corrected to fourteen thousand (μύρια τετρακισχίλια); 'totaled ten' and 'affliction required children to be doubled' replaced by the Greek's 'as the sacred writing says, the children too ought to have been double'; 'contradicting their original number' (not in the Greek) removed; '120 ... 140' replaced by the Greek's 77 and 14.
'were lost' / 'died' keeps Origen's contrast (livestock lost; children died, not lost) and is carried into 'the children he lost' for τῶν ἀπολωλότων παίδων.
Label 'ι ʹ' read as ιϛʹ (verse 16): the stigma was lost in the OCR; the lemma is LXX Job 42:16.

οζʹ (77) for the years of former prosperity conflicts with οηʹ (78) twice in the next section and with the arithmetic (78 x 2 = 156; 78 + 14 + 156 = 248). Not an obvious OCR confusion, so kept as printed with '[below: seventy-eight]'. Reviewer should check the PG column (389).
The lemma gives 240 years in all, the comment 248 (σμηʹ); both translated as printed.
'than they were at first' (ἢ comparative after τριπλᾶ); the stray δὲ is not rendered.
Opens mid-sentence (the protasis 'If the Lord gave Job double ... after the' ends u03-rem-early) and ends mid-sentence; the clause continues in u03-rem-close.

Review 2026-11-11: the bracket '[below: seventy-eight]' was removed from the reading text; οζʹ (77) is translated as printed, and the clash with οηʹ (78) in u03-rem-close is recorded here and in translator_notes.
